Replace.Text: Streamline gameplay by reducing the sources of city bonuses, which can otherwise become hard to keep track of.
Include animal resources for use in supply chains.
Declutter the map by removing modded resources that are not used in supply chains.
Disable pop-up notifications when supply chain effects are added, increased, decreased, or removed. City-panel integration remains available when the MCUIS mod is active.

On new maps, add suitable material deposits to increase favorable placement opportunities for Quarters. Assistance scales with the resource abundance setting. Existing resources remain in place, and continents retain different opportunities.

Help AI civilizations establish Quarters beside Base and Specialty materials, acquire the required tiles, and develop supply chains. Without RomanHoliday's AI, CSC also supplies basic improvement and Builder tuning. With a supported RomanHoliday release enabled, CSC automatically adds supply-chain support to its tuning instead. Turn this off to use the underlying AI without CSC's AI guidance or assistance. Automatic tile acquisition and Quarter foundations currently apply to single-player games.

Use the AI's Gold first. When its safe spending budget cannot cover the next tile toward a Base-and-Specialty Quarter location, fund only the shortfall. With this off, wait until the AI can afford the tile itself. Applies to both CSC basic tuning and RomanHoliday compatibility.
